metadata.laymanSummary: Congress voted on a proposal to replace the current income tax system with a single flat rate of 17% for all Americans, eliminating most deductions.

data.billTitle: Flat Tax Act — Replacing the federal income tax with a 17% flat rate and eliminating the IRS as currently structured

speakers.name: Rep. Jim Jordan
speakers.title: R-OH · House Judiciary Chair
speakers.quote: The current tax code is 77,000 pages long. Nobody understands it. The IRS uses it as a weapon against political enemies. A flat tax of 17% lets every American file on a postcard and eliminates an agency that has become a tool of political persecution.

speakers.name: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
speakers.title: D-NY · House Oversight
speakers.quote: A flat tax is a massive tax cut for the rich and a tax increase for everyone else. A billionaire paying 17% and a teacher paying 17% is not fairness — it is math that benefits the billionaire. This bill would blow a $3 trillion hole in the deficit to give Jeff Bezos a tax break.

speakers.name: Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene
speakers.title: R-GA · House Oversight
speakers.quote: Americans spend 6.5 billion hours a year complying with the tax code. That is time Americans could spend with their families, building businesses, and creating jobs. Simplification is not radical — it is long overdue.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: H.R.1040 failed 187-244. The bill would have replaced all federal individual income tax brackets with a single 17% rate and eliminated most deductions except for a generous personal exemption. The CBO estimated it would reduce federal revenue by $2.9 trillion over ten years. Fifty-seven Republicans joined all Democrats in opposition, citing deficit concerns.

data.title: Should the US replace its tax code with a flat tax?

options.label: No — the deficit impact is too large
